subject: Request: temporary overcommit allowance for Zephyr pilot - autoscale policy exception
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary overcommit allowance for Zephyr pilot - autoscale policy exception

Marcus —

Quick summary: Zephyr Health has a week-long pilot starting 2026-08-10 that will throttle the team into production-like traffic patterns. Based on the early load tests the product team ran, they will need a short-term overcommit on a dedicated pool to keep p95 latency under 300ms for user-facing inference.

Ask: Can we approve a temporary overcommit window (1.5x their reserved capacity) for the pilot week and exempt them from the hard autoscale eviction rule? We think this is the lowest-friction path to demonstrating the SLA uplift and conversion.

Why: Without the extra headroom their requests will get queued and the UX will be poor. Zephyr is Mid-Market and the pilot is tied to a renewal conversation — they’re one of the priority pilots for Q3.

Risks & mitigation we propose in the attached plan (zephyr_pilot_capacity_plan.pdf):
- Limit overcommit to 7 calendar days (2026-08-10 — 2026-08-16)
- Cap cost delta at the estimated amount in cost_delta_estimate.xlsx and require sign-off from finance if exceeded
- Ops runbook for emergency preemption + customer notification (mini-mop-runbook.md)

Can you loop in Capacity/Infra or approve the exception path? Happy to jump on a quick sync.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: zephyr_pilot_capacity_plan.pdf (application/pdf), cost_delta_estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet/xlsx), mini-mop-runbook.md (text/markdown)

Subject: Re: Request: temporary overcommit allowance for Zephyr pilot - autoscale policy exception

Kimberly —

Thanks for the note and the attachments. I skimmed the plan; looks reasonable. A couple quick clarifying Qs before I bring this to infra for a formal exception:
1) Which pool are we proposing to overcommit (pool id / region)?
2) Do we need kernel-level tuning (quantized variant) or is this purely headroom?
3) Who owns customer communication if we get forced preemption?

My initial take: operationally acceptable if we can run strict throttles + an automated fallback to a smaller model variant and keep costs tracked. If Ops signs off, I can route the exception through the temporary-reserve flow and attach a time-bound SLA.

I'll schedule a 30m sync with Ops + Product if that helps — suggest Thu 07/30 10:30am.

—Marcus
Principal Product Manager, Inference Platforms
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary overcommit allowance for Zephyr pilot - autoscale policy exception

Marcus / Kim —

Pool: proposed pool is "us-west-2-dedicated-03" (GPU A100s). Region matched to Zephyr's data residency preference.
Model: product ran on the pruned-13B-q4f16 variant; the performance delta between that and the full 13B is ~8% latency improvement when given additional slots. We do NOT need kernel-level recompile for the window.

Ops ask: If we allow overcommit, we must have these guardrails in place:
- Auto-throttle at 85% sustained for 2 minutes triggers model fallback to pruned-7B variant
- Billing alert to Product & Finance at 120% of baseline reserved spend
- Ops runbook on the first preemption event to contact the SOC on-call and Kimberly's CS lead

I can take the sync on Thu.

Laura Bennett
Senior Product Manager, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

> Marcus / Kim —
> 
> Pool: proposed pool is "us-west-2-dedicated-03" (GPU A100s). Region matched to Zephyr's data residency preference.
> Model: product ran on the pruned-13B-q4f16 variant; the performance delta between that and the full 13B is ~8% latency improvement when given additional slots. We do NOT need kernel-level recompile for the window.

Sounds fine. Operational notes from infra perspective:
- We can provision a 50% temporary overcommit on that pool for the requested week, but we need a hard eviction policy: after 70% sustained utilization for 5m, we start graceful preemption. We will not allow overcommit to exceed 50% of pool capacity without an Exec exception.
- We need a signed cost-acknowledgement from the customer for the delta. Beth Sato from our cloud partner (beth.sato@cloudops.ai) can provide metering hooks if Zephyr signs a short-term top-up addendum.

If Kim and Finance agree on the cost cap, I can book the overcommit slot and enable the tracing hooks for the pilot.

Jonas Weber
Head of Capacity Operations
Redwood Inference
